findings.comment:

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed chlorine sanitizer solution to test at 0 ppm Cl-. Sanitizer solution was remade, and tested at 200 ppm Cl-. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of applesauce and canned items to be stored directly on floor in dry storage area. Store food items at least 6 inches off floor. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, P and shall be used according to manufacturers lable insturctions. The tube carrying sanitizer from the bucket to the machine was pulled out. The tube was replaced and machine primed. Violation corrected.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked by stool with cardboard boxes on it. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11. Boxes were moved immediately.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on inside of milk cooler so that an odor is present when cooler is opened.. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed towel on the drain board of the dish machine. Also observed flocked carpets in the dish area. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. Flocked carpets and towels are not considered easily cleansable surfaces. Remove from the facility.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Observed clean utensils to be stored in mugs on the prep table which are soiled in the bottom with food debris and dust. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. They were removed to dish for proper cleaning.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
. 750.140 - Taco meat prepared this morning was cooling in an ice bath. The date was written on the container, but no time was marked to indicate when the cooling process began. Marking cooling foods with the date and the time was discussed with the Kitchen Manager.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.
**Make sure cooling foods are being stirred frequently and/or rotated with the pan on the ice bath and the temperature is being monitored with a clean, calibrated stem thermometer, to ensure foods are cooling quickly and reaching benchmark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling (135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and 70F to 41F/below w/in 4hrs; total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). Leaving foods uncovered while cooling is allowed in order for steam to vent off as long as the product is stored in a manner that is protected from potential contamination (i.e. no raw foods above cooling foods, shelving above cooling foods must be clean, etc.).**

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Leak was observed along the tubing of the dish machine when the sanitizing cycle was running. Liquid was dripping on top of the detergent bucket from the tubing. Silicone was used to seal around the tubing at the catch basin on front of the machine recently. More silicone is needed in the area. Provide additional repairs to eliminate the leak.

Dish machines shall be properly installed and maintained in good repair. Dish machines shall be operated in accordance with the manufacturers instructions. Automatic dispensers and liquid injectors, if any, shall be properly installed and maintained.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - A) Storm door screen was observed held in place with duct tape. Manager noted the screen falls out otherwise. Custodian stated he can silicone the edge to secure the screen in place. Remove tape and provide proper repairs. Make sure the end result is a tight fitting and vermin proof.

B) Reach-in freezer (next to electrical panel) had frost buildup inside along the door seal and the top shelf. Defrost the freezer.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) Areas of disrepair were noted in the following areas:
1. floor by back door - a. hole near threshold & b. hole in the left corner near floor to wall juncture;  and
2. corner in dish area (plunger storage location) - a. hole in the floor at floor to wall juncture.
Provide repairs in the aforementioned areas. Once repairs are completed the end result must be a smooth, cleanable surface that is easily maintained as such.

B) Floors were soiled in the following areas:
1. under inverted black crates in the corner of storage area (debris/buildup);
2. along the wall next to freezer in storage area  (old glue trap/debris);  
3. between freezer and cooler in storage area (leaves/debris);  and
4. corners in dish area (bottle spray top/debris).
Clean the floor throughout daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris and maintain clean.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Can opener blade had food debris on it. Can opener had not been used during prep up to that point. Can opener was placed in the dish are to go through ware washing process. 

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Pan of hamburger was observed cooling in the 2 door cooler. Date was written on foil, but time was not documented. Employee stated the hamburger was just cooked recently. Surface temperatures were 92F-129F, while the internal temperature ranged from 135F-173F. Pan of hamburger was pulled from the cooler to be portioned and rapidly cooled using an ice bath.

Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F. 
**If cooked foods may be used during service, then a better practice would be to simply hot hold the product in the warmer. Otherwise, proper steps should be taken to properly cool foods (see General Comments).

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee left the kitchen area and did not wash hands prior to putting away clean dishes upon returning to the kitchen. Handwashing was discussed with the employee. Employee properly washed hands prior to moving on to the next task.

Hands must be properly washed prior to working with food, clean equipment, and/or single service articles. Always wash hands upon entering the kitchen before doing any tasks related to food, clean equipment, and/or single service articles.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Can opener blade had a small amount of buildup on one edge of the blade. The crevice around the blade was starting to accumulate metal shavings. The holder had a small amount of food debris on it as well.

Clean and sanitize the can opener and the holder between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of metal shavings and food debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.850 & 860 - Clean ladles were observed with food surfaces extended up out of the storage container. Store utensils with handles presented out of containers so the food contact surfaces are protected from potential contamination during storage and when being retrieved for use.

Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be stored and handled in a way that protects them from contamination. All utensils shall be touched only by their handles. Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 151 - A) Trays of French fries observed on a cart were observed to have surface temperatures of 67F-66F and internal temperature of 65F. Employee stated the fries had been out on trays for ~15 minutes and were pulled from the freezer ~10 minutes prior to being trayed up and placed on the cart. Employee immediately placed fries in the oven for cooking. Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be maintained at proper cold holding temperature of 41F/below until they are ready for steps involving preparation. Once prep is complete, cold PHF must be placed immediately in the oven if cooking is required. If foods will be cooked but are not ready to be placed in the oven then store PHF in coolers until they are ready for use. Do not store PHF at ambient temperature for any length of time. Limit the amount of time PHF spends in the temperature danger zone.
B) Open container of cottage cheese (~1/4 full) was not dated. Employee working at the time was unsure as to when the container was opened. Cottage cheese was discarded in the trash. Date marking of dairy products was discussed at the last routine inspection. All ready to eat, PHF, including non-cultured dairy products (i.e. cottage cheese, 2% milk, etc.), must be marked with the date the original packaging is opened and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date all ready to eat, PHF and do not hold at the facility past 7 days. If the use by dates for non-cultured dairy products fall before the end of the 7 day time frame of the date mark, then go by the use by date for discard. If the use by date is past the 7 day time frame of date mark, then discard unused non-cultured dairy products based on date mark on the 7th day.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.180 & 210 - Philly wraps and cheese sauce were observed in the warmer and had not yet been cooked or reheated. Philly wraps had internal temperature of 126F-128F, and cheese sauce had internal temperature of 134F. Cheese sauce and wraps were placed in the warmer around 8:30a. Philly wraps were being heated for the first time, and cheese sauce was being reheated. All products were immediately placed in the oven to finish properly cooking and reheating to 165F.
The warmer must never be used for stroage of any PHF that has not already been properly cooked or reheated using a piece of equipment intended for cooking/reheating. Warmers are only intended to hold hot foods at 135F/above after they have already reached proper cooking and reheating temperatures. Immediately cease the practice of placing foods in the warmer prior to cooking/reheating. Foods must go from prep and to the oven for cooking/reheating prior to being placed in warmers. 
All potentially hazardous foods shall be cooked to the proper product temperature. PHF shall be reheated rapidly to 165F or higher throughout the product. Properly cook and reheat foods.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Frozen spaghetti sauce was observed thawing at room temperature. Surface temperatures on the sides were at 48F-50F, and surface temperature on the top was at 30F. Product was still fairly frozen and was placed in the 2 door cooler to finish thawing properly. Do not thaw frozen PHF at room temperature. The outside of the product starts to thaw immediately and sits in the temperature danger zone while the inside remains frozen for  much longer. This is a bad practice and must cease immediately. 
PHF shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration at 41F/below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee was observed having bare hand contact with handles of manual faucet and paper towel dispenser once handwashing process was completed. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with employee.
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Have paper towels ready to dry hands. Use paper towels as a barrier to shut off manual faucets and touch handle of paper towel dispenser after handwashing process is complete. If possible, elbows and forearms may be used to touch handles in order to avoid potential re-contamination of freshly washed hands.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Solution used for wiping general surfaces did not contain bleach. Employee stated the kitchen ran out of bleach. More bleach had to be picked up from one of the schools in Auburn and had not happened yet for the day. Maintain a supply of bleach on-site for use in sanitizing solutions. Bleach would also be required for manual sanitizing at the 3 part sink, should there ever been an issue with the dish machine that would require use of the 3 part sink.
Bleach solutions must be maintained at 100-200ppm and used for sanitizing general surfaces.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Worker was observed touching manual faucet and handle of paper towel dispenser with her bare hands after handwashing process was completed. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and educational handouts were provided.
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Have paper towels ready to dry hands, and use paper towels as barrier to shut off manual faucets and touch the handle of the paper towel dispenser after handwashing process is complete.
Common towels are prohibited.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - Edges of wooden shelves in dry storage room had chipped paint and rough wood was exposed. Shelves in question are used for storage of flour, canned fruits, and salsa con queso. Repair (smooth out rough patches & paint) the shelves in the dry storage room. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Bucket of sanitizer solution tested at less than 100ppm chlorine, and the solution was made recently. The water was fairly hot, and soap was also noted to be in the solution. Employee noted a test strip was not used to verify concentration when the solution was made. Staff were advised water that is too hot will cause bleach to dissolve out at an accelerated rate, and soap will neutralize bleach. Solution was to be remade at 100ppm chlorine (w/out soap in the solution) after current food prep was completed. Maintain bleach solutions at 100ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration is correct, and be careful with water temperature/use of soap. **NOTE: Cleaning of in place food contact surfaces would require 3 separate steps of wash (soapy water), rinse (plain water), & sanitize (bleach water at 100ppm).**

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.citation_text: 750.600 - Plastic cinnamon containers were being re-used for storage of sugar and dried onions. Also, what appeared to be an old peanut butter jar (clear container with red lid) had baking powder in it. Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items. Any plastic containers that were purchased with a food product inside (i.e. dry powders, cottage cheese, etc.) are not intended to be re-used for storage of another food when original product is gone. Obtain re-usable containers for food storage (i.e. Ziploc, etc.).

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - (x2) Ants were observed in the dish room under the dish machine around the cleanout cover in the floor at the front of the machine and at the floor to wall juncture around dish machine plumbing where a gap is present. Upon removing the cleanout cover drain flies were observed inside below a yellow rag and a piece of folded black plastic. Thorough cleaning of cleanout (to eliminate drain flies), sealing of all gaps in the immediate area, and use of bait (to minimize number of ants) were discussed with Maintenance worker and Manager. Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 - Gap was present at the floor to wall juncture around dish machine plumbing. Ants were observed crawling in and out of the area. Ants were also observed crawling in and out of a hole where a screw was missing from the cleanout cover in the floor at the front of the machine. Seal the gap around the plumbing and seal the hole of the cleanout cover until the new cover is installed (see general comments). End result must be smooth and easily cleanable. Use of spray foam is not preferred. If expanding foam is used it must be cut down to be flush with the floor and sealed with paint or a clear sealant so the area is smooth and cleanable.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - Large hole was observed in the wall below 2 part sink around water line. Properly repair the wall; end result must be smooth, easily cleanable, and of such material that it can be maintained in a sanitary manner. Walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Some floor tiles at dish machine were noted to be broken/damaged at the 1/10/13 routine inspection. A few tiles by the wall near/around the floor drain are peeling up and/or have a gap. The tiles do not necessarily have to be replaced. Maintenance workers just need to re-seal the loose areas and seal the gaps so the area in question is smooth, easily cleanable, and does not provide a potential hiding place for pests. B) Inside the recessed floor drain at 3 part sink was still soiled in a few areas. Clean the floor drain.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text: 750.830 - Sanitizer concentration at dish machine was 0ppm chlorine upon initial check by inspector. Kitchen staff tried priming and adjusting the hose. Concentration was still below 50ppm. Call for service was made, and repair person is scheduled to come out for repairs today. All dishes ran through the machine today must be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized in the 3 part sink. Kitchen manager stated the primer and hose were replaced in 2012. Re-inspection is scheduled for tomorrow but call will be made prior to re-inspection to verify repairs have been completed. **Kitchen manager was advised on keeping a log for monitoring daily checks of the dish machine since there appears to be an ongoing issue with the machine**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Some floor tiles at dish machine were broken/damaged. Replace the tiles or seal the areas in question so the floor is smooth, easily cleanalble, and does not provide a potential location of harborage for pests. All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by pests. B) Floor drain at 3 part sink was soiled. Clean the floor drain. C) Floor under dry storage shelves holding marshmallows and crackers were soiled with buildup of leaves/debris. Clean the floor in the aforementioned area. Floors and floor drains shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the dishwasher to have no sanitizer when tested with test strips. Repair the dishwasher--Ladies will use the 3 compartment sink til repaired.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed the bulk containers without labeling. (CORRECTED)
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a cloth towel in the dish area with clean dishes stored on top of it. (corrected)
750-660 Food contact surfaces shall be accessible for cleaning and inspection.
